title: Checkbox
description: Checkboxes allow the user to select one or more items from a set.

blocks.text:
Checkboxes can be used to turn an option on or off.

If you have multiple options appearing in a list,
you can preserve space by using checkboxes instead of on/off switches.
If you have a single option, avoid using a checkbox and use an on/off switch instead.

blocks.name: Checkboxes

blocks.text: You can provide a label to the `Checkbox` thanks to the `FormControlLabel` component.

blocks.name: CheckboxLabels

blocks.text: Use the `size` prop or customize the font size of the svg icons to change the size of the checkboxes.

blocks.name: SizeCheckboxes
ColorCheckboxes
IconCheckboxes

blocks.text: You can control the checkbox with the `checked` and `onChange` props:

blocks.name: ControlledCheckbox

blocks.text:
A checkbox input can only have two states in a form: checked or unchecked.
It either submits its value or doesn't.
Visually, there are **three** states a checkbox can be in: checked, unchecked, or indeterminate.

You can change the indeterminate icon using the `indeterminateIcon` prop.

blocks.name: IndeterminateCheckbox

blocks.text:
:::warning
When indeterminate is set, the value of the `checked` prop only impacts the form submitted values.
It has no accessibility or UX implications.
:::
`FormGroup` is a helpful wrapper used to group selection control components.

blocks.name: CustomizedCheckbox

blocks.text: 🎨 If you are looking for inspiration, you can check [MUI Treasury's customization examples](https://mui-treasury.com/primitive/checkbox).

(WAI-ARIA: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/)

- All form controls should have labels, and this includes radio buttons, checkboxes, and switches. In most cases, this is done by using the `<label>` element ([FormControlLabel](/material-ui/api/form-control-label/)).
- When a label can't be used, it's necessary to add an attribute directly to the input component.
  In this case, you can apply the additional attribute (for example `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title`) via the `slotProps.input` prop.

api.name: FormControl
api.description:
Provides context such as filled/focused/error/required for form inputs.
Relying on the context provides high flexibility and ensures that the state always stays
consistent across the children of the `FormControl`.
This context is used by the following components:

 - FormLabel
 - FormHelperText
 - Input
 - InputLabel

You can find one composition example below and more going to [the demos](/material-ui/react-text-field/#components).

```jsx
<FormControl>
  <InputLabel htmlFor="my-input">Email address</InputLabel>
  <Input id="my-input" aria-describedby="my-helper-text" />
  <FormHelperText id="my-helper-text">We'll never share your email.</FormHelperText>
</FormControl>
```

⚠️ Only one `InputBase` can be used within a FormControl because it creates visual inconsistencies.
For instance, only one input can be focused at the same time, the state shouldn't be shared.

api.name: FormGroup
api.description:
`FormGroup` wraps controls such as `Checkbox` and `Switch`.
It provides compact row layout.
For the `Radio`, you should be using the `RadioGroup` component instead of this one.
